source_text: Ceterum Apostolus ostendit, si tamen aliquam ab hominibus hac tempestate fidem impetrat, servos se non dicere peccati nisi eos, quos constat voluntate propria oboedisse peccato, cuius mutatione id est voluntatis coeperunt servire iustitiae; oboedientiam ergo in medio collocavit et ei imputavit, quod vel vitiis prius vel postea studuerunt parere virtutibus.
pass_a_gloss: For the rest the Apostle showed, if nevertheless he obtains any faith from human beings in this season, that he does not call slaves of sin except those who stand as having obeyed sin by their own will, by a change of which, that is of will, they began to serve justice; he therefore placed obedience in the middle and imputed to it that they either first strove to obey vices or afterward virtues.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: The apostle, however—if he can obtain any credibility from people in this age—shows that he calls none slaves of sin except those who are known to have obeyed sin by their own will. By changing that will, they began to serve righteousness. He therefore placed obedience in the middle and attributed to it their effort to obey vices earlier and virtues afterward (compare Romans 6:16–18).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
